[[Providence Park|Multnomah Stadium]] }} {{1960 Western major college football independents records}} The '''1960 Oregon State Beavers football team''' represented [[Oregon State University|Oregon State College]] as an [[Independent (college sports)|independent]] during the [[1960 college football season]]. In their sixth season under head coach [[Tommy Prothro]], the Beavers compiled a 6–3–1 record and outscored their opponents 197 to 145.{{cite web|title=1960 Oregon State Beavers Schedule and Results|publisher=Sports Reference LLC|work=SR/College Football|access-date=September 7, 2016|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/schools/oregon-state/1960-schedule.html}} They played two home games on campus at [[Parker Stadium]] in [[Corvallis, Oregon|Corvallis]] and two at [[Providence Park|Multnomah Stadium]] in [[Portland, Oregon|Portland]]. The [[Pacific Coast Conference]] (PCC) disbanded in 1959; this was the second of five years that Oregon State and [[Oregon Ducks football|Oregon]] competed as independents. The [[Oregon–Oregon State football rivalry|Civil War]] game was played in Corvallis and ended in a tie.{{cite news |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=YxdWAAAAIBAJ&sjid=7eIDAAAAIBAJ&pg=5927%2C3299354 |work=Eugene Register-Guard |location=Oregon |last=Strite |first=Dick |title='Civil War' opponents battle to 14-14 standoff |date=November 20, 1960 |page=1B}} The [[Gotham Bowl]] was scheduled to premiere at [[Yankee Stadium (1923)|Yankee Stadium]] in [[New York City]] in 1960 with [[1960 Holy Cross Crusaders football team|Holy Cross]] as the host team. However, after Oregon State was invited, Holy Cross was uninvited in hopes of finding a better match-up. The game was canceled when no opponent could be found for Oregon State.{{cite news|title=Gotham Bowl inaugural off|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=ZsoUAAAAIBAJ&sjid=6eIDAAAAIBAJ&pg=7072%2C128544 |work=Eugene Register-Guard |location=Oregon |agency=Associated Press |date=December 1, 1960 |page=1D}} After this season, the university's current title, Oregon State University, was adopted by a legislative act signed into law by [[List of governors of Oregon|Governor]] [[Mark Hatfield]] on March 6, 1961, and became effective that summer.{{cite news |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=XP9VAAAAIBAJ&sjid=0uIDAAAAIBAJ&pg=2154%2C807741 |work=Eugene Register-Guard |location=Oregon |agency=Associated Press |title=OSU measure signed by Gov.
